content.title: Tigers smash Padres in 8-2 Opening Day win, McGonigle 4-for-5 in debut
content.text: Updated March 26, 2026, 7:03 p.m. ETIt's officially Tigers season, and the 2026 season has started out hot.The Detroit Tigers (1-0) beat the San Diego Padres (0-1) 8-2 on Thursday, March 26, at Petco Park in San Diego. The game was highlighted by rookie Kevin McGonigle, who batted 4-for-5 with two doubles and two RBIs in a highly productive debut.McGonigle started his MLB career with a two-RBI double in the top of the first inning, jumping on the first pitch he saw to drive in left fielder Riley Greene and first baseman Spencer Torkelson. He followed that with another double in the third inning and an infield single in the fifth, before finishing his day with a two-out single in the ninth inning.Watch Detroit SportsNet on FuboLefty ace Tarik Skubal pitched efficiently through six innings, allowing one unearned run and striking out six batters over 74 pitches.Here's how it all went down. Kevin McGonigle: 'I dreamed of this'In his first MLB post-game interview, Kevin McGonigle said that he had an MLB debut he has "dreamed" of."It hit me [during] that flyover right before the game, it's hard to put into words," he told Detroit SportsNet's Daniella Bruce after the game. "It was a dream my whole life, and I'm living in it right now. I'm still taking it all in." Tigers win 8-2FINAL: Tigers 8, Padres 2.Tigers closer Will Vest shut down the Padres in the ninth inning to finish the game. The Tigers win 8-2 and start the season 1-0. Kevin McGonigle gets fourth hitMiddle 9th: Tigers 8, Padres 2.Kevin McGonigle has had a debut for the ages.With a two-out single into right center field, McGonigle is now 4-for-5 with two doubles and two singles in his MLB debut. Drew Anderson final lineEnd 8th: Tigers 8, Padres 2.Appearing in two innings in his Tigers debut, reliever Drew Anderson was taken out midway through the eighth inning. He finished 1⅓ innings of work with two hits, one earned run on a home run, two walks and zero strikeouts.Lefty Tyler Holton entered the game for Anderson and loaded the bases on a two-out walk to designated hitter Miguel Andujar, but got pinch hitter Nick Castellanos to fly out to center field to strand the runners. Drew Anderson allows home run in Tigers debutEnd 7th: Tigers 8, Padres 2.Drew Anderson's debut as a Detroit Tiger (and the righty's first MLB appearance since 2021) went well to start the seventh inning, but then left fielder Ramón Laureano sent a changeup over the left field wall for a two-out, solo home run, making the game 8-2.Anderson got second baseman Jake Cronenworth to ground out to end the seventh. Tarik Skubal final lineBottom 7th: Tigers 8, Padres 1.After 74 pitches and six innings, Tigers ace Tarik Skubal has been removed from the game, replaced by righty Drew Anderson.Skubal's final line: 6 innings pitched, 3 hits, 1 run (not earned), zero walks and six strikeouts. Tarik Skubal allows first run of his startMiddle 6th: Tigers 8, Padres 1.Padres shortstop Xander Bogaerts doubled on a 2-1 changeup from Skubal, scoring Fernando Tatis Jr. from first base. Since Tatis initially reached on a throwing error from Javier Báez, the run is unearned for Skubal.The lefty finished the inning with consecutive strikeouts on third baseman Manny Machado and center fielder Jackson Merrill. Through six innings, Skubal has allowed three hits, zero earned runs and has struck out six. Javier Báez makes first challenge of the seasonMiddle 5th: Tigers 8, Padres 0.Shortstop Javier Báez took an 0-1 fastball off the plate that was initially called a strike. Báez then challenged the pitch, which was overturned and ruled a ball, giving him a 1-1 count.He capitalized immediately with a two-out single, not only overturning the call but parlaying it into a base hit. A good result for Detroit's first challenge of the season. Dillon Dingler hits home runTop 5th: Tigers 8, Padres 0.Tigers catcher Dillon Dingler has Detroit's first home run of the season.A no-doubter off the ribbon scoreboard in left field, Dingler's home run scored McGonigle from first base and gave the Tigers an 8-0 lead. Kevin McGonigle 3-for-3Top 5th: Tigers 6, Padres 0.With one out in the top of the fifth, McGonigle hit a cue shot towards Padres shortstop Xander Bogaerts and beat out an infield single. Though his third hit wasn't nearly as hard as his first two, McGonigle is 3-for-3 in his MLB debut. Tarik Skubal cruising through four inningsEnd 4th: Tigers 6, Padres 0.After an easy second inning, Skubal set the Padres down in order for an efficient third inning, thought left fielder Riley Greene made an awkward catch on the warning track on a hard line drive from shortstop Xander Bogaerts.His fourth inning went much the same, with Skubal getting three quick outs on seven pitches. Skubal has four strikeouts on 42 pitches through four innings. Parker Meadows gives Tigers 6-0 leadMiddle 3rd: Tigers 6, Padres 0.Center fielder Parker Meadows hit a bloop single into shallow left field to score both Spencer Torkelson from third base and Kevin McGonigle from second.The Tigers have a 6-0 lead in the middle of the third inning. Kevin McGonigle hits another doubleTop 3rd: Tigers 4, Padres 0.Two MLB plate appearances, two doubles for Kevin McGonigle.First baseman Spencer Torkelson hit a 3-2 fastball into left-center field for a leadoff single to open the third inning, and McGonigle smoked a 2-2 fastball off the wall in the right field corner, missing a home run by just a few feet.It's his second double of the game. Tarik Skubal strikes out two in the 2ndEnd 2nd: Tigers 4, Padres 0.Skubal got Padres left fielder Ramón Laureano to strike out on a low changeup to record his second strikeout of the game. One batter later, Skubal brought catcher Freddy Fermin to the same result. Tigers down on three fly ballsMiddle 2nd: Tigers 4, Padres 0.Right fielder Kerry Carpenter and second baseman Gleyber Torres both flew out to begin the first inning, though Torres almost snuck on base when Padres right fielder Fernando Tatis Jr. appeared to lose the ball in the sun before making an athletic catch at the wall.After designated hitter Colt Keith hit a two-out single, left fielder Riley Greene just missed a hanging curveball and flew out to left field. Tarik Skubal pitches out of one-out jamEnd 1st: Tigers 4, Padres 0.Tigers starter Tarik Skubal picked up a swinging bunt from right fielder Fernando Tatis Jr. and shoveled it to first baseman Spencer Torkelson to record the first defensive out of the season for the Tigers. Shortstop Xander Bogaerts followed that with a single, and third baseman Manny Machado followed that hit with a bloop single into shallow center field that moved Bogaerts to third base.Skubal then got center fielder Jackson Merrill to strike out on a check swing on a changeup in the dirt on a favorable call for the Tigers. Designated hitter Miguel Andujar then hit a hard ground ball to second baseman Gleyber Torres, but Torres vacuumed it up and completed the groundout to get Skubal out of the jam. Dillon Dingler drives in a runMiddle 1st: Tigers 4, Padres 0.One pitch after McGonigle hit and RBI double in the first plate appearance of his MLB career, Tigers catcher Dillon Dingler hit a ground ball in between shortstop and third base to drive in first baseman Spencer Torkelson from third base.After, center fielder Parker Meadows and shortstop Javier Báez both struck out, ending a four-run first inning for the Tigers. Kevin McGonigle makes MLB debut with RBI doubleTop 1st: Tigers 3, Padres 0.The first plate appearance of Kevin McGonigle's career leads to runs.McGonigle jumped on the first pitch he saw and drove it down the right field line for a two-RBI double, extending the Tigers lead to three runs early in the first. Spencer Torkelson drives in first run of the seasonTop 1st: Tigers 1, Padres 0.The first Tigers RBI of the season goes to first baseman Spencer Torkelson, who drove in second baseman Glebyer Torres on a four-pitch, bases-loaded walk. Tigers load bases early onTop 1st: Tigers 0, Padres 0.After right fielder Kerry Carpenter struck out on three pitches to start the game, Tigers second baseman Gleyber Torres took a one-out walk. On the next pitch, Colt Keith blooped a single into left field, putting runners on first and second with one out.Left fielder Riley Greene then watched a 3-2 curveball bounce to earn a one-out walk to load the bases, bringing first baseman Spencer Torkelson up to bat. San Diego weatherIt brings us no pleasure to inform you that it is 74 degrees and sunny in San Diego right now.As for Detroit, maybe don't look out the window ... Tigers wearing grayFor those of you hoping the Tigers would wear their alternate blue road uniform to start the season, you will have to wait at least a day. The Tigers are wearing gray today. Hinch has revealed his Opening Day lineup.RF Kerry Carpenter (L).2B Gleyber Torres (R).DH Colt Keith (L).LF Riley Greene (L).1B Spencer Torkelson (R).3B Kevin McGonigle (L).C Dillon Dingler (R).CF Parker Meadows (L).SS Javier Báez (R).Tarik Skubal is set to pitch for the Tigers. Tarik Skubal's third-straight Opening Day startTigers starter Tarik Skubal is making his third-straight Opening Day start today against the Padres. He's the first Tigers pitcher to make at least three-straight starts on Opening Day since ... his teammate, actually.Tigers time vs Padres for Opening DayDate: Thursday, March 26.Time: 4:10 p.m. ET.Location: Petco Park, San Diego.Tigers channel vs Padres for Opening DayAll three games of the Tigers' upcoming series against the Padres will be broadcasted locally on Detroit SportsNet.Channel: Detroit SportsNet.Time: 4:10 p.m. ET.Streaming: MLB App, Fubo.Radio: WXYT-FM (97.1).Watch Tigers Opening Day on FuboWhere is Detroit SportsNet on my TV package?Comcast/Xfinity: 1253.DirecTV: 663.Spectrum/Charter (Alpena, Detroit, Duluth-Superior, Flint-Saginaw, Grand Rapids-Kalamazoo, Lansing, Marquette, Traverse City): 213.Spectrum/Charter (Livonia): 291Spectrum/Charter (Fort Wayne, Green Bay-Appleton, Toledo): 307/1307.Spectrum/Charter (on Spectrum app): 436.Tigers pitching matchup vs Padres for Opening DayDET: LHP Tarik Skubal (13-6, 2.21 ERA in 2025).SDP: RHP Nick Pivetta (13-5, 2.87 ERA in 2025).Tigers vs Padres series scheduleThe first series of the regular season for the Tigers will have different start times for all three games.Thursday: 4:10 p.m. ET (DSN).Friday: 9:40 p.m. ET (DSN).Saturday: 8:40 p.m. ET (DSN).Is Jason Benetti announcing Tigers-Padres Opening Day?No, but it's not because he's no longer part of the team. Benetti will be calling the Los Angeles Dodgers vs. Arizona Diamondbacks game for NBC after signing a new deal with the company. He will still be fulfilling his role as play-by-play man for the majority of Tigers games, but will be absent on most Sunday broadcasts, calling "Sunday Night Baseball."How much will Detroit SportsNet cost?Fans can pay $19.99 per month or $189.99 for a full year – approximately $50 cheaper over a 12-month span. Fans can learn more about streaming subscriptions for the Tigers and Red Wings at Tigers.com/detroitsportsnet and DetroitRedWings.com/detroitsportsnet.How to stream Tigers and Red Wings games?The new streaming home for the Tigers is the MLB app, available on web, mobile and TV platforms – with access to highlights, stats and news. As for the Red Wings, a system to stream games for the 2026-27 season is yet to be announced.This article included contributions from Free Press sports editor Andrew Birkle.Need to catch up on the news during your lunch break?
